REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 25, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments will be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.

Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a legislative body member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition,
verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
SEPTEMBER 25, 2025, 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

With the exception of Item 9A, all agenda items were held concurrently with the Thursday,
September 25, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council Special Meeting agenda. Details for the Special
Meeting Agenda items are provided on the Thursday, September 25, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City
Council Special Meeting Minutes.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 394.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Albano’s Plumbing Inc. (Business Spotlight).

  Shirley Garcia (100th birthday).

  Association of Latino Professionals for America, Cerritos College; and Immigrant
  Student Alliance, Cerritos College (National Hispanic Heritage Month).

  Cerritos-Artesia Rotary Club (Service Clubs Month).

  Robert A. Lopez, City Manager, introduced a video presentation as part of the City’s
  Strategic Plan progress toward Goal 4 – Strengthen Economic Development, and Goal
  7 – Improve Community Communications. A brief social media video reel highlighting
  the grand opening of the Chubby Cattle restaurant was displayed.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, September 25, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  Informational presentation by the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County
  Clerk (County) on the Tuesday, November 4, 2025 Statewide Special Election.

  The item was introduced by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk/Elections Official. An
  informational presentation was given by Adrian Avelar, Policy and Program
  Compliance Division, Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

5C.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal ad
  hoc working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was deferred to the
  next City Council/Successor Agency meeting agenda (scheduled for Monday, October
  13, 2025).

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Benjamin Ao expressed concern regarding the verbiage included in the Oath of Office
  administered to elected and appointed officials in the City of Cerritos, requesting the
  City include verbiage required by Federal law, for public officials.

  Teddy Lloyd offered suggestions for revenue generation and economic development,
  including pickleball events and partnerships with local universities.

  City Attorney, Pam Lee, noted the distinction between required language for oaths of
  office administered to Federal public officials under United States Code (5 U.S.C. §
  3331) and State of California (CA Constitution, Article XX, Section 3) oath of office
  language requirements, for oaths administered to State and local public officials.

  David Pylman expressed concern regarding modification to the City Council meeting
  regular schedule and requested Agenda Item 7C be pulled from the Consent Calendar
  for separate consideration.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members
  received full-text, unredacted copies of five (5) written comments submitted for Item
  6 (inclusive of one (1) comment for Item 5A), by the deadline listed on the agenda
  and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments
  submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office of
  the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider New and
Old Business Item 9A prior to consideration of Agenda Item 7. Consent Calendar.

  Account/Project: cp22505 Regional Stormwater Capture Facility Project

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  David Pylman expressed concern regarding a change of the City Council Regular
  Meeting schedule and inquired as to City Attorney availability for the proposed,
  modified meeting schedule. He also expressed concern regarding noticing related to
  various community organization meetings, given the recent elimination of the printed
  and mailed version of the Cerritos News.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
